_comment: Pinned schema provenance for partition anchor eligibility (issue #73).
An op anchors an island only when a RESIDENT constant initializer sits at one of the
schema-designated weight sites listed here. This file is the single source of truth the
Rust `weight_site_indices`/`is_heavy_family` tables and the docs are checked against by
`ci/check_anchor_weight_sites.py`. It is machine-checked, not hand-trusted: standard-domain
rows are re-extracted live from the pinned `onnx` schema library, and contrib rows are
verified against the pinned ORT commit recorded in third_party/onnxruntime/PROVENANCE.md.
A `weight_sites` of [] means the op is heavy-family (FLOP-significant) but designates NO
weight site, so it can never anchor on its own (e.g. GroupQueryAttention).

onnx.note: Standard-domain input names/order are extracted live from onnx.defs by the checker; the indices below must match the operand position of the named weight input for the schema version resolved by the pinned onnx package.

onnxruntime.note: com.microsoft contrib op schemas are not registered in onnx.defs, so their weight-site provenance is pinned to the exact ORT source lines below at the commit above. The checker fails closed if the vendored commit changes without re-pinning.

ops.provenance: onnx.defs MatMul (A, B); right-hand matrix B is the weight.
onnx.defs Gemm (A, B, C); B is the weight, C the optional bias.
onnx.defs Conv (X, W, B); W is the kernel weight.
onnx.defs ConvTranspose (X, W, B); W is the kernel weight.
onnx.defs Attention (Q, K, V, ...): operands are already-projected activations; no resident weight site. Heavy-family, non-anchor.
ORT onnxruntime/core/graph/contrib_ops/contrib_defs.cc:3672-3686 @ da9b5e3; Input(1, "B") is the packed int-N weight. Doc: 'the right-hand-side matrix (weights) is quantized to N bits'.

ORT onnxruntime/core/graph/contrib_ops/bert_defs.cc:1258-1332 @ da9b5e3; all operands are runtime activations, KV cache, or rotary/scale tensors. The q_norm_weight/k_norm_weight inputs (idx 14/15) are per-head RMS-norm scales, NOT a projection weight matrix, and are deliberately excluded — this is why the designation is an explicit index list, not a name-substring heuristic. Heavy-family, non-anchor.
ORT contrib op; operands are projected Q/K/V and biases, no resident projection weight matrix. Heavy-family, non-anchor. Fail-closed default until a weight site is pinned.

ORT contrib op with a weights input in some variants; weight-site provenance not pinned in this revision, so it is left as the fail-closed default (no anchor). Not in any currently censused model. Pin the index with provenance before relying on it to anchor.
ORT contrib op carrying quantized expert weights; input order not pinned in this revision, so left as the fail-closed default (no anchor). Not in any currently censused model.
ORT contrib op; weight-site provenance not pinned in this revision, fail-closed default (no anchor). Not in any currently censused model.
